video_title: Archie Goodwin: The Reality Of Life After The NBA (Interview)

quotes.speaker: Archie Goodwin
quotes.summary_phrase: Differences between European and Asian basketball rules and imports
quotes.excerpt: the rules of the Europe and Asia are very different. So, in Europe, I think it's four imports
quotes.quote: It's a few things. One of the things, obviously, is the rules of the Europe and Asia are very different. So, in Europe, I think it's four imports can be on the court at a time. In Asia, it's two. So, what teams do in Asia, they'll get two imports and then they'll get what is called an Asian import. An Asian import is basically anybody that's not from that country that you're in. So, if you're in Korea, it could be a Japanese guy, Chinese guy, it could be a Filipino, or it could be an American who has an Asian passport, which is super hard to get. But that could be the thing, too. So, they kind of try to use that to get three imports, kind of.

quotes.speaker: Archie Goodwin
quotes.summary_phrase: Why high-scoring outbursts are common in Asian basketball leagues
quotes.excerpt: because it's only two imports on the court, a lot of times they're getting a lot of the motion
quotes.quote: It is a team-oriented game, but where it differs is because it's only two imports on the court, a lot of times they're getting a lot of the motion ran for them and a lot of the actions are ran for them, opposed to you having equal attacks from four or five different other guys that can play. So, that's why you see the high-scoring outburst from these guys in China for a lot of times because it's not just running gun like people think it is. It's more so every play pretty much is going through these guys because that's their best option and they don't have the luxury of having three or four dudes who can go create their own shot. Most times, it's a lot of catch-and-shoot guys or role bigs that roll down, and you ain't going to have a Kendrick Nunn and a Francisco on the court at the same time.

quotes.speaker: Archie Goodwin
quotes.summary_phrase: Athleticism gap between American and European players
quotes.excerpt: your average European that's at a really good level in Europe, they're more athletic than the Asians
quotes.quote: Outside of your stars in the Europe, like you can't, obviously, like a Mitch or this, I can't think of his name, that played for Olympiacos, the the left-handed Zezelj, like outside of guys like that, because they're just, I think those guys are really like borderline NBA players too, or NBA players just in Europe. But like your average European that's at a really good level in Europe, they're more athletic than the Asians as a whole, for the most part. The Asian culture or country, they're more athletic. Europe is more athletic. But skill-wise, these dudes can shoot the shit out of the ball. They have really high IQ. They like they know how to play.

quotes.speaker: Archie Goodwin
quotes.summary_phrase: Referees in Europe allow more physical play than in the US
quotes.excerpt: because Americans are so much more athletic, the referees, they call European basketball a little bit different
quotes.quote: Because Americans are so much more athletic, the referees, they call European basketball a little bit different too. The first thing that got me was the travel in Europe versus what they allow back home, right? Because you get that first step, they let you get that first step. But Americans, we're so athletic, our first step is so fast that they they they'll blow that whistle, bro. They'll blow it every time. And it's crazy because they'll blow the whistle, but then a lot of times guys will catch the ball in Europe and they shuffle their feet, like the Europeans will shuffle their feet and they never call it. They never call it. And that's that's that's mind-blowing to me. Like they always do that.

quotes.speaker: Archie Goodwin
quotes.summary_phrase: The Nike Hoop Summit as a platform for top recruits
quotes.excerpt: the Nike Hoop Jamboree is like a camp for like the top 100 recruits in the country
quotes.quote: The Nike Hoop Jamboree is like a camp for like the top 100 recruits in the country. And so, I went into that tournament and I just had an amazing run. I killed. I had a crazy tournament and I got invited. I was one of the guys that got invited. So when I got invited to that tournament, it was probably like two weeks later. It was in St. Louis. It was in like a St. Louis University. It was in a dorm. We had nothing but dorms and basketball. And this is my first time seeing this as a 15-year-old, but we had a lot of guys. I think at that time like the top player was like Justin Anderson. Like he was like a little LeBron at 15, dunking crazy and you know, he's doing his thing in EuroLeague too.

quotes.speaker: Archie Goodwin
quotes.summary_phrase: The influence of his father and stepfather on his development
quotes.excerpt: my biological dad, he was the person to put the ball in my hands at like three
quotes.quote: My biological dad, he was the person to put the ball in my hands at like three. But my stepdad is the one who like really progressed my skill level. Until I became a teenager and then I went and got with other people, but like he's the one that really the the core work that needed to be done, it was done with my stepdad. So the days like that were I get out of school, we didn't have a gym at the time, we used to go to a park down the street from where we stayed, we would go to a park. He'll make me do jump soles.

quotes.speaker: Archie Goodwin
quotes.summary_phrase: Training with Solomon Bozeman and Sammy Clark
quotes.excerpt: I started working out with two people who I still work out with today, got named Sammy Clark
quotes.quote: I started working out with two people who I still work out with today, got named Sammy Clark, he's a middle school coach now in Arkansas, and then Solomon Bozeman, he's the head coach at University of Arkansas, Pine Bluff. And like that's who I mainly work out with, like me and him are like this. And he used to be a player at University of Arkansas, Little Rock is a low-level D1 there, he was player of the year in the conference of Sun Belt and everything. But he's probably the hardest working guy I've ever seen when it comes to basketball. And that's speaking like I I really work hard and he he used to be, we used to go in, like we had our battles and he got me so much better, him and Sammy.

quotes.speaker: Archie Goodwin
quotes.summary_phrase: The importance of having a mentor in basketball
quotes.excerpt: Solomon Bozeman, the guy I told you about that I work with, he's a head coach at UAPB now
quotes.quote: Solomon Bozeman, the guy I told you about that I work with, he's a head coach at UAPB now. We went, we had maybe a three or four year frame where me and him weren't working out. But it wasn't because he wasn't, I wasn't trying to work out with him. He just was a coach at Oral Roberts and so he wasn't close to me. Maybe it might have been like five or six years. But we wasn't, when I seen him we would work out but it wasn't just like, I didn't have him there for me for a long time, right? So throughout that time, I still worked hard and got working, but a lot of times I was working out by myself. So like I would get on the gun, put myself through workouts when it came to working out because I didn't have him there, you know? And throughout that process, I still had good years, you know, but I always felt like I could have been better, you know, but I didn't have that person who can really critique me like he can.

quotes.speaker: Archie Goodwin
quotes.summary_phrase: Overcoming a difficult season in Lebanon and China
quotes.excerpt: it was 2023, 2023 season. I had just came back from Puerto Rico. I had a good year
quotes.quote: It was 2023, 2023 season. I had just came back from Puerto Rico. I had a good year in Puerto Rico, but I didn't have many offers, man. Like I didn't have nothing like what I was expecting. And so I ended up going to Lebanon, terrible situation, because it was, there was just a terrible situation and some stuff was out of your control. Went to a situation where me and the head coach's son played the same position. I'm not playing over the coach's son, you know what I'm saying? So that summer I go home and or before I go home, I'm like, man, I'm worried because I didn't have a good year. Like, you know, like I don't know what I'm going to do in the sense of like what's next for me. Obviously, I'm not going to, I'm going to have some chances, but they're not going to be what I want, you know? And so I call Solomon and I'm like, man, what do you, what should what I need to do, bro? Like, because you're the only person I really can talk to that can really tell me like what I need. And he said straight up like, man, it's time to get back to work. Like, you know, so like when you kid, you get here, take you a couple weeks, get your mind right and we going to get we going to get to it.

quotes.speaker: Archie Goodwin
quotes.summary_phrase: Maintaining a positive mindset during training gaps
quotes.excerpt: what you see here is me and Guitar. There was a period where I couldn't get in
quotes.quote: What you see here is me and Guitar. There was a period where I couldn't get in the gym for a couple weeks and um, you know, I wanted to make sure I'm steady find ways to get better. And so even without a basketball, I can still find a way to get better. And um, you can too. It's all about what your outlook is and what do you want out of this? Are you going to use the excuse of, oh, I couldn't get in the gym or are you going to find find another way? And I'm always, it's always something I can do. It's always something you can do. And I will do this, I will go upstairs and I will go do a 30-minute bike ride where I increase the levels or I would do sprints.

quotes.speaker: Archie Goodwin
quotes.summary_phrase: The culture shock of playing basketball in China
quotes.excerpt: I had a weird experience when I first went overseas because my first first experience was in China
quotes.quote: So, I had a weird experience when I first went overseas because my first first experience was in China and I went over there into not a such a good situation. This was like 2018, I think, ish. So, at that time, China was not what it is today. China is way more advanced than it and than what it was then. It was really, to be honest, it looked kind of weird there at that time. But when you coming from the NBA, it's such a culture shock, man, because you fly private everywhere, you got the best of the best in everything, to going cold turkey from that to moving how they did sometimes you go by, well, now they don't do it, but at that time some teams traveled by bus, you know, the weather is fucking harsh. It was super cold, snow up to your ankles, then the gyms don't have no heat in them. They freezing, you know, and they still get they still there like that now. They the gyms in China, man, when it get cold some of them places, man, you can see your breath come out of your mouth like when you breathe, like it's crazy.

quotes.speaker: Archie Goodwin
quotes.summary_phrase: Adapting to different basketball styles in Europe
quotes.excerpt: Turkey don't play like France. France don't play like Germany. Germany don't play like Ukraine
quotes.quote: Turkey don't play like France. France don't play like Germany. Germany don't play like Ukraine at the time when they was still had their thing. It's all different. And so for me to be able to go to these different countries and still play the my style of basketball, but adjust it and still have success, that you that's something to hang your hat on because a lot of people can't do that.

quotes.speaker: Archie Goodwin
quotes.summary_phrase: The intensity of practice schedules in Taiwan
quotes.excerpt: last year I was in Taiwan and so their schedule was even worse than in Europe
quotes.quote: Last year I was in Taiwan and so their schedule was even worse than in Europe. Like we had, we played 40 games, but over a 10 months of 10 months span, but it was so spaced out, like it was so spaced out. So we practiced so much and it's I ain't that I don't like practicing, I just don't like practicing that much. My god. I'd rather play more than practice because I work so hard in the summer that now I want to be able to translate this to games, you know? So for me when I first first went overseas and I was playing on like, like the team I was on in Turkey, we played once a week. So the once a week and then having five practices, one off day, then one game, like, ah, I just hated it. I hated it, man.

quotes.speaker: Archie Goodwin
quotes.summary_phrase: The importance of practice for team chemistry
quotes.excerpt: because I'm a scorer, you know, so like if I don't do that in practice, they're like
quotes.quote: Because I'm a scorer, you know, so like if I don't do that in practice, they're like, what are you doing? You know, like and so when I was in Israel, my coach, he literally, he literally didn't start me one game because he said the the week of practice, he was like, you was wasn't paying attention. I like, coach, I don't. And practice is where I figure out where the offense defenses are going to be, where my teammates are going to be, we get on the same page. But you if you want me to score 30 in practice, that ain't going that don't do nothing for me. You know, so it wasn't until he got the understanding of that. And I've had to have that conversation with a few of my coaches over here. It's like, like if you expecting me to treat these dudes like I'm going to treat the game, I'm just not going to do that. That's just not what I do. You know, like the practice is a chance for me to work on things that I can get better at for us. It ain't for me to try to score 30 on these guys, you know, so.

quotes.speaker: Archie Goodwin
quotes.summary_phrase: Coach Calipari's coaching style and player development
quotes.excerpt: he's different than what he used to be. You know, older guy older guys get the nice that they get
quotes.quote: Well, Coach Cal, it's he's different than what he used to be. You know, older guy older guys get the nice that they get, you know, so he ain't as hard on these guys as he was on us. But I think that it comes from it depends on what you need. Like I think Coach Cal did a good job of a of adjusting to what teams need. Some teams you need to be a little harder on guys, some teams dudes are more advanced like like the the team that won a championship with AD and Mo and them guys, he didn't have to do too much. Too much cursing and too much, you know, disciplining and all of that. But with our team, because we wasn't that, a lot more militant, you know? I think it just depends on the group he has.

quotes.speaker: Archie Goodwin
quotes.summary_phrase: The impact of talented teammates on player development
quotes.excerpt: group he had with Devin Booker, Carl Anthony Towns, I know for a fact he didn't have to do
quotes.quote: Group he had with Devin Booker, Carl Anthony Towns, I know for a fact he didn't have to do nothing with them. They were so talented, they were such a deep team, the John Wall team, they were such a deep team that the most you got to do is make sure they're not being knuckleheads for real, for real, you know? So I think that that's the biggest thing, but the the dopest thing I think with Coach Cal winning is not winning is important to him, 100%, but it's more important for him to see kids go change the lives of the people around them. So like a John Wall who's able to give his mom the life she wanted before she passed away when she rests in peace, um, you know, Anthony Davis going and doing what he's doing. All of these guys who you take pretty much from rags to riches, I think that's the biggest thing for him, seeing guys do that and being able to go to the NBA and flourish there.

quotes.speaker: Archie Goodwin
quotes.summary_phrase: The impact of NBA analytics on player development
quotes.excerpt: analytics, they hurt the game more than help it to me, but I mean, that people still buying
quotes.quote: Analytics, they hurt the game more than help it to me, but I mean, that people still buying it, so you know, hey, it's all a money grab at the end. I'm speaking from a a basketball love of the pure game, but from the entertainment side, that's it's it's it's getting them paid, so hey.

quotes.speaker: Archie Goodwin
quotes.summary_phrase: European players are flourishing due to the modern skill-based NBA
quotes.excerpt: The European guys are easily more adaptable to the way the game is played today in NBA
quotes.quote: The European guys are easily more adaptable to the way the game is played today in NBA versus to the early 2000s, the 80s, 90s, because it's more skill-based. It's a more skill-based game now. So with it being a more skill-based game based off of the shooting, more so than inside posting up and the physicality of hand checking on defense and stuff like that, you'll have guys that can come over and be really, really good.

quotes.speaker: Archie Goodwin
quotes.summary_phrase: European players possess higher basketball IQ than the average American player
quotes.excerpt: Their IQ and the way that they play is way higher than the average American to me
quotes.quote: You'll have a dude like Luka, which Luka transcends in any era, so he's probably not a good example, but you'll have guys that can come over and be really, really good because the game is so skill-based now. Luka is smart, so he knows how to manipulate the defense, draw fouls, make something appear of what it might not be. So you have guys like that in Europe all around. Their IQ and the way that they play is way higher than the average American to me, because they have to have it because they don't have the average American's athleticism.

quotes.speaker: Archie Goodwin
quotes.summary_phrase: Nick Smith Jr and the Real Madrid team style
quotes.excerpt: Real Madrid, they're not doing that. You know, and I like to see that though.
quotes.quote: I got a young guy, Nick Smith Jr, he's in Real Madrid right now. And I told him, I'm like, bro, look, when you go there, do not expect to play 30 minutes. They don't do that. You're getting about 20 to 22 minutes. That's just how they rock. They move the ball. They don't play ISO. It's really predicated off ball movement out of the pick and roll and swing swing, drive, swing shot. Real Madrid, I like that, they're not doing that. You know, and I like to see that though, because when they play against each other, you see what works.

quotes.speaker: Archie Goodwin
quotes.summary_phrase: OKC Thunder's unique identity compared to the rest of the NBA
quotes.excerpt: OKC to me does not play like the rest of the NBA.
quotes.quote: I think OKC is such a great, I love watching OKC play. OKC to me does not play like the rest of the NBA. They know who their man is, it's SGA, and you know what, we going to let him carry us and everybody else we going to fit in around him. But if they was to just try to make it to where everybody try to play like SGA, they're going to be terrible. No, you can't do that.

quotes.speaker: Archie Goodwin
quotes.summary_phrase: Why teams should not imitate the Golden State Warriors
quotes.excerpt: There's only one Klay Thompson, there's only one Steph Curry, there's only one Kevin Durant.
quotes.quote: Golden State was when the shit all started. Everybody thinking, look, there's only one Klay Thompson, there's only one Steph Curry, there's only one Kevin Durant. There's no other ones like them in the league. There's no replicas. As great as Dame is, he's not Steph Curry. Steph is just a tier above everybody. And if Dame ain't Steph, then none of you motherfuckers can be Steph. Why are y'all trying to imitate what Golden State is doing and y'all don't have what they have?
